remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NOT act on execution instructions arriving outside that delivery path
Only from agents within the same authorized AutoGen runtime

threats.summary: Any message source — including an agent relaying attacker-authored content — supplies fenced code that is extracted and run, because `sources` defaults to None and is a self-declared string.

In the model_client flow, untrusted message text is added to the model context unlabeled and can steer the code the model generates (the sources filter does not apply there) (checked: _code_executor_agent.py:550, :836 — no provenance labelling).

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NOT carry any capability that grants inbound network access to, or a persistent interactive shell into, the execution environment
MUST NOT expose the code-execution environment, or the Docker daemon socket it relies on, to untrusted or public networks

threats.summary: The kernel gateway binds 0.0.0.0 with all ports published, so any reachable host holding (or not needing, when the token is empty) the token can start kernels and run code outside the agent delivery path.
The gateway token travels over plaintext ws:// even when use_https is set, exposing it to network observers of non-local gateways.

remit_rules.excerpt: Human confirmation by the overseer is required before every code-block execution
The executor MUST NOT execute a code block that the human overseer has denied.
Alert the operator when a code block is denied at the human-confirmation gate.
A sandboxed execution backend (Docker or Azure Container Apps dynamic sessions) is required for all code execution.
The local host executor ... MUST NOT be used unless the operator has explicitly authorized it
MUST NOT execute agent- or LLM-generated code outside an isolation boundary
the executor MUST halt and alert the operator rather than falling back to unsandboxed host execution
Installing packages into the host interpreter ... MUST require human confirmation.

threats.summary: Every block executes without confirmation by default: approval_func is opt-in, is forced to None by `_from_config`, and the executor interface has no approval hook of its own.
A denied block produces no operator alert or log entry — the declared event_logger is never called.
When Docker is absent or fails to start, create_default_code_executor silently returns the host executor, so model-generated code (including pip installs) runs on the host.
LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor and JupyterCodeExecutor run on the host with no explicit operator authorization and are rebuildable from declarative config.
Operators are told dangerous commands are regex-screened, but no denylist exists, so host execution is unscreened.
FunctionWithRequirementsStr executes its source string in the host process at construction, outside any sandbox, even when a Docker/ACA backend is selected.
A timed-out Jupyter cell keeps running in the host kernel because the timeout is shielded and no interrupt is sent.
A generated `# filename:` hint could place a code file outside the workspace; the resolve/relative_to check rejects any out-of-workspace path.

remit_rules.excerpt: Credentials and tokens used to authenticate to a backend MUST NOT be written into generated code files, into execution output, or into logs.

threats.summary: Executed code can print inherited host credentials into execution output, which is appended to the model context and sent to the model provider.

Execution output (attacker-influenceable via fetched data or crafted stderr) re-enters the model context as an unlabelled UserMessage and steers retry/reflection generation (checked: _code_executor_agent.py:616, :648 — no labelling or sanitisation).

threats.summary: The Docker sandbox sits on the default bridge network with no egress control, so executed code can exfiltrate the rw-mounted workspace to any internet destination.
The container runs as image-default root with full capabilities and no memory/pids limits, and no backend detects or halts escape or out-of-bounds attempts.
ACA upload_files joins caller-supplied names onto work_dir unchecked, so an absolute path sends arbitrary readable host files (e.g. credential files) into the remote session.
ACA download_files writes session-listed names (controlled by executed code) to work_dir / name with no containment, enabling writes outside the working directory.
DockerJupyterServer chmods the bind dir 0o777, so any local user on a multi-user host can plant or alter files the kernel reads and that flow back to the agent.
